source.name: WMO State of the Climate 2025 Update and UNEP Coastal Flood Exposure

cadence: Annual WMO global-climate update and UNEP coastal-exposure assessment review.
provenance: Official WMO observed global mean sea-level rates and current low-lying-coast exposure paired with UNEP current additional 1-in-20 annual coastal-flood exposure. Observation, exposure and projection boundaries remain separate.
uncertainty: Low-lying-coast and coastal-flood exposure depend on elevation, population, protection and hazard models. Preliminary 2025 sea-level data are affected by natural variability. Exposure is not realized annual displacement or loss.
failure_behavior: Retain the last reviewed assessment pair and mark stale; reject changed periods, probabilities or population boundaries. Never add overlapping exposed populations, treat exposure as annual victims or score future projections as current impact.

assessment.geographic_scope: global low-lying coasts and coastal communities
source_locators: WMO State of the Climate 2025 Update: nearly 11 percent of the global population, around 900 million people, live on low-lying coasts directly exposed to coastal hazards.
WMO State of the Climate 2025 Update: sea-level rise rate increased from 2.1 mm/year in 1993-2002 to 4.1 mm/year in 2016-2025.
UNEP: coastal-flood extent increased over 20 years, leaving 14 million more people with a 1-in-20 annual flooding chance.
